bugs.creator: traversc
bugs.summary: Bug with CHARSXP lifetime assumption by ALTSTRING elt method

comments.creator: traversc
kevinushey
comments.text: One clean way to solve this problem: add the created CHARSXP vectors to R_VStack, so that their lifetime is at least as long as the typical strings produced by translateChar and friends. I've attached a patch.

To justify why R should be responsible for managing the lifetime of a produced CHARSXP from an ALTREP class here:

Neither side can see the boundary that matters. The class can't observe when a caller is done with an element, and the caller can't observe how it was produced. So the only contract a class can implement alone is "keep every element I've ever returned alive as long as the vector" -- materialization over time, exactly what lazy classes exist to avoid. (Cheaper schemes like retaining the last element in data2 fail against pmatch(), which holds pointers to every element of both arguments at once.)

The evaluation scope is the other natural boundary, and only R can see it: anchoring Elt results on the R_alloc stack gives element pointers the same lifetime as translateChar() results, and class-side anchoring becomes a performance choice rather than a safety requirement.

For concreteness, two prominent ALTREP string implementations on CRAN have exactly this shape today. vroom's string_Elt on a not-yet-materialized column returns the CHARSXP freshly created in Val() -- protected only during construction, then unprotected and returned, stored nowhere (vroom_chr.h#L48-L84; unchanged in 1.7.1).

arrow's AltrepVectorString::Elt does the same on its unmaterialized path, returning a bare Rf_mkCharLenCE() result (altrep.cpp#L861-L887), and is used by default for string columns. I verified the vroom case end-to-end under an ASan build of unpatched trunk: substr() on a lazy vroom column reports heap-use-after-free, with the freed CHARSXP allocated by vroom_chr::Val via ALTSTRING_ELT and freed by GC inside mkCharLenCE() while do_substr still held a pointer into it. With this patch applied, the identical script against the identical vroom binary runs clean. (arrow I confirmed at the source level only -- same structure, same dispatch path -- as building libarrow under ASan isn't practical.)
comments.creator: kevinushey

comments.text:
That's an elegant solution, it took me a while to understand it. It has the right semantics, but my concern is overhead. If you have to allocate a node for every string element, that can get heavy in terms of memory usage.

I have an open PR on vroom that would fix it at the package level: https://github.com/tidyverse/vroom/pull/638. The PR could be improved in terms of memory usage, but you can see it would be easier to do so directly in vroom itself. And on top of that, a package level fix can act as a cache for materialization, which would be another performance improvement.

So I still think the ideal solution is enforce it at the package level on CRAN, where cost is easier to amortize. There are lots of contractual obligations for packages on CRAN and this would be no different.
